events.note: Three months and ten days (2 Chronicles 36:9).
events.why: Theographic's 3M10D is two units in one; the Bible's three months and ten days, as days.
Theographic's 2.5Y is not a whole number of years; the same, in months.

events.why: Christadelphian terminology: ecclesia means the assembly of believers; the Holy Spirit is the power of God (Acts 2:17-18).

events.why: Christadelphian terminology: ecclesia means the assembly of believers; the Holy Spirit is the power of God (Acts 2:17-18).

events.why: Christadelphian terminology: ecclesia means the assembly of believers; the Holy Spirit is the power of God (Acts 2:17-18).

events.title: Jesus tempted in the wilderness
events.note: The adversary (satan) is a delegation of the Jewish leaders, the generation of vipers (Matthew 3:7; 12:34). Having seen his baptism, they come to him in the wilderness of the Jordan valley above the Dead Sea, by Beth-arabah, after his forty days of fasting, and offer him the kingdoms of the land, the tetrarchies of Israel, if he will lead them as their king. Matthew gives the order: the wilderness, the pinnacle of the temple, then a high mountain.
events.why: Christadelphian reading of the temptations, split into its three places; see the journey of the same name.

events.note: Luke 10:38 leaves the village unnamed. Bethany is the working identification from John 11:1, and its placement among the later Judean episodes follows the harmony.
This is a meeting of the chief priests and Pharisees (John 11:47-53), not a recorded visit by Jesus to their council.
Jesus meets the man in Jerusalem and sends him to wash in Siloam (John 9:6-7). The man, not Jesus, is explicitly said to go to the pool. The encounter location within Jerusalem is unknown.
Expanded into individual appearances, including John 21. This spans the forty days before the ascension (Acts 1:3), rather than all occurring on resurrection day.

events.why: Theographic's verses run from Exodus 6:7, through the plagues, which are now their own event.

events.why: Theographic's one event for Joshua 4-12 is divided: the camp at Gilgal here, then Jericho, Ai, Gibeon and Merom, Haqor's own events.

events.why: Holy Week is the church calendar's name; Scripture does not name the span, from the entry into Jerusalem to the resurrection.

added.title: Set on the pinnacle of the temple
added.note: Taken up to Jerusalem and set on the pinnacle of the temple: its south-west corner, where the priest stood to blow the trumpet for the sabbath; the stone inscribed "to the place of trumpeting" fell from it. "Cast thyself down": a sign to the people, answered from Deuteronomy 6:16.

added.title: Shown the kingdoms from a high mountain
added.note: A high mountain: Pisgah, where Yahweh shewed Moses all the land (Deuteronomy 34:1–4), and where Balak took Balaam to view Israel, offering him honour (Numbers 22:17; 23:14). The kingdoms offered are the tetrarchies of Israel; "Get thee hence" sends the adversary away (Deuteronomy 6:13).

added.title: Jesus ministers in the Judean countryside
added.note: Jesus and his disciples leave Jerusalem for Judean country. His disciples perform the baptisms (John 4:2); Aenon in John 3:23 is John the Baptist's location. The lower-Jordan point is a geographical estimate.

added.title: Jesus returns through Sidon
added.note: The critical-text reading takes the return from Tyre through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee through Decapolis. The KJV reads departure from the coasts of Tyre and Sidon. The point represents the district, not a proved visit to the city centre.

added.title: Jesus returns beyond Jordan
added.note: After Dedication Jesus returns to where John first baptized and remains there. Bethany beyond Jordan is a working identification from John 1:28, distinct from Bethany near Jerusalem.

added.title: Mighty works in Chorazin
added.note: Jesus' rebuke presupposes earlier mighty works in Chorazin, but neither an individual episode nor its date or itinerary is narrated. This node records that retrospective evidence without an invented chronological edge.

added.title: Jesus appears to Mary Magdalene
added.note: Near the empty tomb; the Holy Sepulchre vicinity is the working estimate.

added.title: Jesus meets the women leaving the tomb
added.note: On their way from the tomb. A nearby point represents the encounter; its precise position and relation to John's Mary appearance are uncertain.

added.title: Jesus walks to Emmaus
added.note: Jesus joins two disciples on the road and enters Emmaus. The village identification is uncertain; the return to Jerusalem in verse 33 is the disciples' journey.

added.title: Jesus appears to the gathered disciples
added.note: Jerusalem that evening. Reusing the supper-room vicinity is an estimate: the texts do not identify this meeting room as the Last Supper room.

added.title: Jesus appears with Thomas present
added.note: Eight days later. The location is inferred as the disciples' Jerusalem lodging; John does not name the house.

added.title: Jesus meets the disciples by the Sea of Tiberias
added.note: Jesus stands on the shore, provides breakfast and speaks to Peter. The exact beach is unnamed; a northwestern-shore estimate is used in the journey notes.

added.title: Jesus commissions the disciples on a Galilean mountain
added.note: The mountain is unnamed. Its relation to the John 21 appearance is left unordered.

added.title: Jesus leads the disciples out and ascends
added.note: Toward Bethany on the Mount of Olives. Acts 1:3 supplies forty days; Luke's compressed narrative is not used to date the ascension to resurrection evening.

added.title: Jesus appears to Simon Peter
added.note: The disciples report an appearance to Simon before the gathering of Luke 24:36. No setting is described; Jerusalem is a working regional estimate, not an identified meeting site.

added.title: Jesus taken first to Annas
added.note: Estimated in the affluent Upper City, near the high-priestly quarter, for John 18:13-24. No house of Annas has been securely identified.

added.title: Jesus sent to Caiaphas
added.note: Working estimate on the southeastern edge of the Upper City, near the traditional high-priestly site. Matthew 26:57 names the host, not the street or building; this identification is uncertain.

added.title: Jesus brought before the morning council
added.note: Estimated in the Upper City near the high-priestly residences for the morning council (Luke 22:66). The Gospel does not identify its chamber; no route into the Temple precinct is asserted.

added.title: Jesus brought to Pilate
added.note: Herod's western palace is the working identification of the governor's headquarters (John 18:28-19:16; Mark 15:16). The Antonia fortress is an alternative tradition. The exact trial courtyard is uncertain.

added.title: Pilate sends Jesus to Herod
added.note: Estimated at the traditional Hasmonean-palace area in the Upper City for Luke 23:7-12. His presence in Jerusalem is explicit; his lodging is not named.

added.title: Herod returns Jesus to Pilate
added.note: Herod's western palace is the working identification of the governor's headquarters (John 18:28-19:16; Mark 15:16). The Antonia fortress is an alternative tradition. The exact trial courtyard is uncertain.

added.title: Abram rescues Lot; Melchizedek blesses him
added.note: Lot is taken captive from Sodom. Abram pursues the kings from Mamre to Dan, and smites them as far as Hobah, north of Damascus; returning, he is met by Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of the most high God, and gives him tithes.

added.title: Abraham sojourns in Gerar
added.note: Abraham journeys from Mamre toward the south and sojourns in Gerar, where Abimelech takes Sarah and is warned in a dream.

added.title: Hagar and Ishmael sent away
added.note: At Isaac's weaning Hagar and Ishmael are sent away, and wander in the wilderness of Beersheba until God shows Hagar a well.

added.title: Abraham's covenant with Abimelech at Beersheba
added.note: Abraham and Abimelech swear an oath over a well, and the place is called Beer-sheba, the well of the oath.

added.title: Abraham offers Isaac on Mount Moriah
added.note: From Beersheba to the land of Moriah, the third day, where the temple was later built (2 Chronicles 3:1). Yahweh provides the ram, and swears to bless Abraham's seed, in whom all nations shall be blessed (Galatians 3:16).

added.title: Death of Sarah; the cave of Machpelah
added.note: Sarah dies at Hebron, aged 127, and Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah before Mamre from the sons of Heth: his only possession in the land of promise.

added.title: Isaac sojourns in Gerar
added.note: In the famine Yahweh tells Isaac not to go down into Egypt, and renews the oath sworn to Abraham. Isaac sojourns in Gerar, digs again his father's wells, and goes up to Beersheba, where he too makes a covenant with Abimelech.

added.title: Jacob takes Esau's blessing
added.note: At Beersheba Jacob, by his mother's counsel, receives the blessing of the firstborn, and is sent away to Padan-aram to take a wife of Laban's daughters, out of Esau's reach.

added.title: Jacob's dream at Bethel
added.note: Going out from Beersheba toward Haran, Jacob sleeps at Luz and sees the ladder set up on the earth; Yahweh gives him the land and the promise made to Abraham and Isaac, and he calls the place Bethel.

added.title: Jacob serves Laban for Leah and Rachel
added.note: At the well of Haran Jacob meets Rachel, serves Laban seven years for her, is given Leah, and serves seven more for Rachel.

added.title: Jacob leaves Laban; the covenant of Galeed
added.note: After twenty years Jacob flees with his household; Laban overtakes him in mount Gilead, and they raise the heap Galeed and the pillar Mizpah between them.

added.title: Jacob wrestles at Peniel
added.note: The angels of God meet him at Mahanaim. At the ford Jabbok he wrestles until daybreak and is named Israel, and calls the place Peniel: I have seen God face to face.

added.title: Jacob meets Esau and settles at Shechem
added.note: Esau runs to meet him and they are reconciled. Jacob builds a house at Succoth, then comes to Shechem, buys a field, and raises an altar, El-elohe-Israel.

added.title: Dinah and the men of Shechem
added.note: Shechem the son of Hamor defiles Dinah; Simeon and Levi slay the men of the city.

added.title: Jacob returns to Bethel
added.note: Jacob's household put away their strange gods; at Bethel God appears to him again, confirms the name Israel, and renews the promise of the land.

added.title: Jacob goes down to Egypt
added.note: At Beersheba God tells Jacob, Fear not to go down into Egypt; I will go down with thee. Joseph meets him in Goshen, and he stands before Pharaoh, a hundred and thirty years old.

added.title: The burning bush at Horeb
added.note: Keeping Jethro's flock, Moses comes to Horeb, the mountain of God, in Midian; Yahweh declares his name, I AM THAT I AM, and sends him to bring Israel out of Egypt.

added.title: Moses before Pharaoh; the plagues
added.note: Moses returns from Midian, meets Aaron at the mount of God, and asks Pharaoh to let the people go; the plagues fall on Egypt, and Goshen is spared.

added.title: Crossing the Red Sea
added.note: Led by the pillar of cloud by the way of the wilderness of the Red sea, Israel camps before Pi-hahiroth and passes through the sea on dry ground; Pharaoh's host is drowned. The song of Moses.

added.title: The bitter waters of Marah; Elim
added.note: Three days without water, then the bitter waters of Marah made sweet by the tree; then Elim, with twelve wells and seventy palm trees.

added.title: Manna in the wilderness of Sin
added.note: The people murmur for bread; Yahweh gives quails at evening and manna in the morning, and the sabbath rest.

added.title: Water from the rock; Amalek at Rephidim
added.note: Moses smites the rock in Horeb and the place is called Massah and Meribah; Joshua defeats Amalek while Aaron and Hur hold up Moses' hands.

added.title: Jethro visits Moses at the mount of God
added.note: Jethro brings Zipporah and her sons to Moses where he camped at the mount of God, and counsels him to appoint judges.

added.title: The spies sent from Kadesh
added.note: Twelve spies search the land as far as Hebron and the brook Eshcol; ten bring an evil report, and the generation is turned back into the wilderness for forty years. Joshua and Caleb alone are spared to enter.

added.title: Water from the rock at Meribah; Miriam dies
added.note: In the first month of the fortieth year, at Kadesh, Miriam dies; Moses smites the rock twice and is barred from bringing the congregation into the land.

added.title: Aaron dies on Mount Hor
added.note: Aaron's garments are put on Eleazar his son, and Aaron dies in the top of the mount, by the border of Edom, aged 123.

added.title: Sihon and Og overthrown
added.note: Israel takes Heshbon, the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, and smites Og king of Bashan at Edrei.

added.title: Balaam blesses Israel
added.note: Balak brings Balaam to the high places of Baal, to the top of Pisgah and to the top of Peor to curse Israel camped in the plains of Moab; he blesses them three times, and foretells the Star out of Jacob.

added.title: Moses' words in the plains of Moab
added.note: On this side Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses declares the law again, and gives Joshua the charge to lead Israel over.

added.title: Jericho falls
added.note: Seven days round the city, the seventh day seven times; the wall falls flat, and Rahab and her household are saved.

added.title: Ai taken; the covenant at Ebal
added.note: Achan's sin brings defeat at Ai; after judgment in the valley of Achor, Ai is taken by ambush. Joshua builds an altar on mount Ebal and reads the law, half the people over against mount Gerizim.

added.title: Gibeon; the sun stands still
added.note: The Gibeonites gain a league by deceit; the five kings of the Amorites besiege Gibeon, and are chased by the way of Beth-horon while the sun stands still upon Gibeon.

added.title: The northern kings at the waters of Merom
added.note: Jabin king of Hazor gathers the kings of the north at the waters of Merom; Joshua smites them suddenly and burns Hazor.

added.title: The tabernacle at Shiloh; the land divided by lot
added.note: The congregation sets up the tabernacle at Shiloh, and Joshua casts lots before Yahweh for the seven tribes that remain; he is given Timnath-serah in mount Ephraim.

added.title: Joshua's covenant at Shechem
added.note: Joshua gathers the tribes to Shechem: choose you this day whom ye will serve; as for me and my house, we will serve Yahweh.

added.title: Samuel born and called at Shiloh
added.note: Hannah of Ramathaim-zophim prays at Shiloh for a son and lends him to Yahweh; the child Samuel ministers before Eli, and Yahweh calls him in the night.

added.title: The ark among the Philistines
added.note: The ark is carried from Ebenezer to the house of Dagon at Ashdod, then to Gath and Ekron, plaguing each; the kine bring it back to Beth-shemesh, and it rests at Kirjath-jearim twenty years.

added.title: Samuel judges Israel at Mizpeh
added.note: Israel puts away the Baalim at Mizpeh; the Philistines are thundered upon, and Samuel sets up the stone Ebenezer. He judges Israel year by year in circuit to Bethel, Gilgal and Mizpeh, returning to Ramah.

added.title: Saul anointed by Samuel
added.note: Seeking his father's asses, Saul comes to Samuel's city in the land of Zuph and is anointed. His signs: two men by Rachel's sepulchre at Zelzah, three at the plain of Tabor, and the company of prophets at the hill of God.

added.title: Saul made king at Mizpeh; Jabesh-gilead saved
added.note: Saul is chosen by lot at Mizpeh; he relieves Jabesh-gilead from Nahash the Ammonite, and the kingdom is renewed at Gilgal.

added.title: Jonathan at Michmash
added.note: Saul offers the burnt offering at Gilgal without Samuel; Jonathan and his armourbearer climb to the Philistine garrison at Michmash, and the host flees.

added.title: Saul rejected after Amalek
added.note: Saul spares Agag and the best of the spoil, sets up a monument at Carmel, and at Gilgal Samuel tells him, to obey is better than sacrifice: Yahweh has rejected him from being king.

added.title: David anointed at Bethlehem
added.note: Samuel anoints the youngest son of Jesse, the shepherd, in the midst of his brethren.

added.title: David flees from Saul
added.note: From Naioth in Ramah to Nob and the shewbread, to Achish at Gath, the cave Adullam, Keilah, the wildernesses of Ziph and Maon, and En-gedi, where David spares Saul's life.

added.title: David at Ziklag
added.note: Achish king of Gath gives David Ziklag; the Amalekites burn it while he is away, and he recovers all.

added.title: Saul and the woman of Endor
added.note: With the Philistines gathered at Shunem, Saul goes by night to a woman with a familiar spirit at Endor.

added.title: David king in Hebron
added.note: The men of Judah anoint David king in Hebron, where he reigns seven years and six months; then all the tribes come to him there.

added.title: David takes Jerusalem; the ark brought up
added.note: David takes the stronghold of Zion, the city of David, and brings up the ark from Baale of Judah, that is Kirjath-jearim, dancing before Yahweh.

added.title: David and Bathsheba; Nathan's parable
added.note: While Joab besieges Rabbah, David takes Bathsheba and has Uriah slain; Nathan tells him, Thou art the man.

added.title: Absalom's revolt
added.note: Absalom is made king in Hebron; David flees Jerusalem over the Kidron and up the mount of Olives, weeping, past Bahurim where Shimei curses him, to Mahanaim, where he hears of Absalom's death.

added.title: The threshing floor of Araunah
added.note: After the numbering of the people and the pestilence, David buys the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite and builds an altar: mount Moriah, where the temple was built (2 Chronicles 3:1).

added.title: Solomon anointed at Gihon
added.note: Adonijah exalts himself at En-rogel; at David's word Zadok and Nathan anoint Solomon at Gihon, riding on the king's mule.

added.title: Solomon's dream at Gibeon
added.note: At the great high place of Gibeon Solomon asks for an understanding heart, and is given riches and honour also.

added.title: Naomi and Ruth return to Bethlehem
added.note: In the days when the judges ruled, a famine drives Elimelech and Naomi from Bethlehem to Moab. Widowed, Naomi returns with Ruth the Moabitess, who gleans in the field of Boaz; Boaz redeems the inheritance and marries her, and their son Obed is David's grandfather. Boaz is the son of Rahab (Matthew 1:5), which sets this early in the judges.

added.title: Reign of Nabopolassar
added.note: The Chaldean who made Babylon free of Assyria, father of Nebuchadnezzar. With the Medes he destroyed Nineveh. The Bible does not name him; dated as historians date him, from the Babylonian Chronicles.

added.title: Reign of Cyaxares
added.note: King of the Medes, who joined Nabopolassar to take Nineveh in 612. The Bible does not name him; dated after Herodotus.

added.title: Fall of Nineveh
added.note: The Medes and the Babylonians take Nineveh, as Nahum and Zephaniah foretold: "he will make Nineveh a desolation" (Zephaniah 2:13). Assyria's last king flees to Haran, and Pharaoh Necho goes up to help him, killing Josiah at Megiddo on the way (2 Kings 23:29).

added.title: The seventy years of servitude to Babylon
added.note: "These nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years" (Jeremiah 25:11): from the first captivity, in the third year of Jehoiakim, to the first year of Cyrus and his decree, "until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths" (2 Chronicles 36:21).

added.title: Jehoiakim bound; the first captivity
added.note: In the third year of Jehoiakim Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem, binds the king in fetters, carries part of the vessels of the house of God to the house of his god, and takes of the king's seed and the princes, Daniel among them. Jehoiakim serves him three years, then rebels.

added.title: Daniel and his companions in the king's service
added.note: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, children of Judah without blemish, are taught the learning and tongue of the Chaldeans for three years and renamed Belteshazzar, Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego. Daniel will not defile himself with the king's meat; at the end they are found ten times better than all the magicians. "And Daniel continued even unto the first year of king Cyrus" (1:21).

added.title: Battle of Carchemish
added.note: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim Nebuchadnezzar routs Pharaoh Necho by the river Euphrates (Jeremiah 46:2). "The king of Egypt came not again any more out of his land" (2 Kings 24:7). His father dying that summer, Nebuchadnezzar hastens back to Babylon to take the throne.

added.title: Reign of Nebuchadnezzar
added.note: From his father's death in 605 to his own in 562, as historians date him. His first year was the fourth of Jehoiakim (Jeremiah 25:1). "Thou art this head of gold" (Daniel 2:38): to him and his son and his son's son the nations were given to serve (Jeremiah 27:7).

added.title: Nebuchadnezzar's dream of the image
added.note: In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar: the image of gold, silver, brass, iron and clay, and the stone cut out without hands that breaks it and becomes a great mountain filling the whole earth. The God of heaven will set up a kingdom which shall never be destroyed. Daniel is made ruler over the province of Babylon.

added.title: Jehoiachin carried to Babylon; the second captivity
added.note: At the return of the year Nebuchadnezzar takes Jehoiachin with his mother, princes, mighty men and craftsmen, ten thousand captives, Ezekiel and Mordecai's family among them, and the treasures of the house of Yahweh; he makes Mattaniah king, renaming him Zedekiah. Ezekiel counts his years from this captivity.

added.title: Jeremiah's letter to the captives
added.note: Sent to those carried away with Jeconiah: build houses, plant gardens, seek the peace of the city; "after seventy years be accomplished at Babylon I will visit you" (29:10). Placed in the year of Jeremiah 28, the fourth of Zedekiah; the letter itself is undated.

added.title: Reign of Astyages
added.note: The last king of the Medes; his own army gave him up to Cyrus in 550. The Bible does not name him; dated after Herodotus.

added.title: The image of gold and the burning fiery furnace
added.note: Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego will not worship the image set up in the plain of Dura; cast bound into the furnace heated seven times, they walk loose in the fire with a fourth "like a son of the gods", and not a hair is singed. The Hebrew gives no year; the Greek reads the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, the year before Jerusalem burned.

added.title: The siege of Jerusalem
added.note: On the tenth day of the tenth month, in the ninth year of Zedekiah, Nebuchadnezzar comes against Jerusalem and builds forts round about it; the same day Ezekiel is told of it in Babylon (Ezekiel 24:2). The siege runs to the eleventh year, until famine prevails in the city.

added.title: Jerusalem and the house of Yahweh burned
added.note: On the ninth of the fourth month of Zedekiah's eleventh year the city is broken up; Zedekiah flees by night, is taken in the plains of Jericho, sees his sons slain at Riblah and is blinded and bound for Babylon. In the fifth month, in Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year, Nebuzaradan burns the house of Yahweh, the king's house and every great house, breaks down the walls, and carries away the rest of the people.

added.title: Gedaliah slain; the remnant flee to Egypt
added.note: In the seventh month Ishmael son of Nethaniah, of the seed royal, murders Gedaliah, whom Nebuchadnezzar had made governor at Mizpah. Against Jeremiah's word the remnant go down into Egypt for fear of the Chaldeans, taking him with them to Tahpanhes.

added.title: Ezekiel hears that the city is smitten
added.note: In the twelfth year of the captivity, on the fifth of the tenth month, one that had escaped out of Jerusalem comes to Ezekiel saying, "The city is smitten", and his mouth is opened.

added.title: The third captivity
added.note: In the three and twentieth year of Nebuchadnezzar Nebuzaradan carries away 745 persons of the Jews: in all, Jeremiah counts 4,600 taken in the three deportations he numbers.

added.title: Nebuchadnezzar driven out seven times
added.note: The dream of the great tree hewn down, its stump left in the earth: boasting of great Babylon that he had built, Nebuchadnezzar is driven from men to eat grass as oxen until seven times pass over him, till he knows that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men. Daniel gives no year; placed late in his reign, after his building of Babylon (4:30), the kingdom restored to him before his death (4:36).

added.title: Reign of Evil-merodach
added.note: Amel-Marduk, Nebuchadnezzar's son, killed in 560 by Neriglissar, his sister's husband.

added.title: Jehoiachin lifted up out of prison
added.note: In the seven and thirtieth year of his captivity, in the twelfth month, Evil-merodach in the year he began to reign brings him out of prison, sets his throne above the kings that were with him, and gives him a continual allowance all the days of his life.

added.title: Reign of Neriglissar
added.note: Nergal-sharezer, Nebuchadnezzar's son-in-law: very likely the Nergal-sharezer, Rab-mag, who sat in the middle gate of Jerusalem when it fell (Jeremiah 39:3, 13). His young son Labashi-Marduk reigned a few months after him.

added.title: Reign of Cyrus
added.note: King of Anshan in Persia from 559, of the Medes from 550, of Lydia from 547 and of Babylon from 539, to his death in 530. Named by Isaiah as Yahweh's shepherd and anointed, who would say to Jerusalem, Thou shalt be built, a century and a half before (Isaiah 44:28; 45:1).

added.title: Reign of Nabonidus
added.note: The last king of Babylon, father of Belshazzar. For ten years from his third year he lived at Tema in Arabia, leaving the kingship in Babylon to his son. The Bible does not name him; dated as historians date him, from the Nabonidus Chronicle.

added.title: Reign of Belshazzar
added.note: Nabonidus's eldest son, entrusted with the kingship in Babylon from his father's third year while Nabonidus was at Tema: so Daniel could be made only the third ruler in the kingdom (Daniel 5:16, 29). Slain the night Babylon was taken.

added.title: Daniel's vision of the four beasts
added.note: In the first year of Belshazzar: four great beasts out of the sea, the lion, the bear, the leopard and the dreadful fourth beast with ten horns and a little horn; the Ancient of days sits, and one like the son of man is given the kingdom, which the saints of the Most High take and possess for ever.

added.title: Cyrus takes the kingdom of the Medes
added.note: Astyages' army deserts to Cyrus and Ecbatana falls: the Medes and the Persians are one kingdom, Persia the higher of the ram's two horns, which came up last (Daniel 8:3, 20).

added.title: Daniel's vision of the ram and the he-goat
added.note: In the third year of Belshazzar, at Shushan by the river Ulai: the ram with two horns pushing westward, northward and southward, broken by the he-goat from the west; the great horn broken and four coming up; the little horn waxing great toward the pleasant land; and "unto two thousand and three hundred days; then shall the sanctuary be cleansed" (8:14).

added.title: Belshazzar's feast: the writing on the wall
added.note: Drinking from the vessels of the house of God, Belshazzar sees the fingers of a man's hand write upon the wall: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN. Weighed in the balances and found wanting, his kingdom divided and given to the Medes and Persians. Daniel is clothed with scarlet and made third ruler; that night Belshazzar is slain.

added.title: Babylon taken by the Medes and Persians
added.note: On the sixteenth of Tishri (12 October 539), Cyrus's army enters Babylon without battle, the river's passages stopped, as Isaiah and Jeremiah foretold, and the gates left open before him (Isaiah 45:1). Cyrus himself enters some days later.

added.title: Reign of Darius the Mede
added.note: The son of Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes, who took the kingdom at about threescore and two years old and was made king over the realm of the Chaldeans (Daniel 5:31; 9:1). The Babylonian records name no king of Babylon so between Nabonidus and Cyrus: he is identified with Gubaru, whom Cyrus set over Babylon, or with Cyaxares son of Astyages, Cyrus's uncle, as Xenophon tells. Two years, before the first year of Cyrus (Ezra 1:1), after Jones.

added.title: Daniel in the den of lions
added.note: Set first of the three presidents over the 120 princes, Daniel still prays three times a day toward Jerusalem against the king's decree, and is cast into the den of lions; his God sends his angel and shuts the lions' mouths. Darius writes to all the earth to tremble before the God of Daniel.

added.title: Daniel's prayer: the seventy weeks
added.note: In the first year of Darius, understanding by Jeremiah's books that the seventy years of Jerusalem's desolations were near accomplished, Daniel confesses the sins of his people. Gabriel brings the seventy weeks determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, unto Messiah the Prince.

added.title: Cyrus's decree: the house of God to be built
added.note: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of Yahweh by Jeremiah might be fulfilled, Cyrus proclaims through all his kingdom that the Jews may go up to build the house of Yahweh at Jerusalem, and brings out the 5,400 vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken, to Sheshbazzar the prince of Judah. Dated 536 after Jones, at the end of the seventy years; historians date Cyrus's first year in Babylon to 538.

added.title: The first return under Zerubbabel and Jeshua
added.note: The children of the province go up, every one to his city: the whole congregation together 42,360, besides 7,337 servants and maids and 200 singing men and women, with Zerubbabel and Jeshua the high priest at their head.

added.title: The altar built; the feast of tabernacles kept
added.note: When the seventh month is come the people gather as one man to Jerusalem; they set the altar upon his bases and offer the burnt offerings morning and evening, and keep the feast of tabernacles, though the foundation of the temple is not yet laid.

added.title: Daniel's last vision by the Hiddekel
added.note: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia: the kings of Persia and Grecia, the king of the north and the king of the south, the time of trouble, and the resurrection: "many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake" (12:2). "Go thou thy way till the end be: for thou shalt rest, and stand in thy lot at the end of the days" (12:13). When he died is not recorded; the bar runs to an estimated ninety years.

added.title: The foundation of the house of Yahweh laid
added.note: In the second month of the second year of their coming: the people shout with a great shout, but many of the priests and Levites, ancient men who had seen the first house, weep with a loud voice, so that the noise of the joy cannot be discerned from the weeping.

added.title: The work on the house of God ceases
added.note: Refused a part in the building, the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin weaken the hands of the people and hire counsellors against them all the days of Cyrus, even until the reign of Darius; the work ceases unto his second year, while the people dwell in their cieled houses and the house lies waste.

added.title: Reign of Cambyses
added.note: Cyrus's son, who added Egypt to the empire in 525. The Bible does not name him; dated as historians date him.

added.title: Reign of Darius I
added.note: Darius son of Hystaspes, "the Great": in his second year the building of the house of God resumed, and it was finished in his sixth (Ezra 4:24; 6:15). Defeated by the Greeks at Marathon in 490.

added.title: Haggai and Zechariah stir up the building
added.note: In the second year of Darius Haggai asks, "Is it time for you to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste?" Yahweh stirs up the spirit of Zerubbabel, of Joshua and of all the remnant, and on the twenty-fourth of the sixth month they come and work in the house.

added.title: Tattenai's letter; Darius finds Cyrus's decree
added.note: Tattenai, governor beyond the river, writes to Darius asking who commanded the building; the roll of Cyrus's decree is found at Achmetha, and Darius commands that the work go on at the king's expense, and that whoever alters the word have his house pulled down.

added.title: The house of God finished and dedicated
added.note: Finished on the third day of the month Adar, in the sixth year of Darius, through the prophesying of Haggai and Zechariah: dedicated with joy, a hundred bullocks, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and twelve he-goats for a sin offering for all Israel.

added.title: The passover kept in the new house
added.note: On the fourteenth of the first month the children of the captivity keep the passover, with all that had separated themselves from the filthiness of the heathen of the land, and the feast of unleavened bread seven days with joy.

added.title: Reign of Ahasuerus (Xerxes)
added.note: Xerxes I, son of Darius, reigning from India to Ethiopia over 127 provinces (Esther 1:1): the fourth king, far richer than they all, who by his riches stirred up all against the realm of Grecia (Daniel 11:2), and was defeated at Salamis in 480.

added.title: Accusation against Judah in the reign of Ahasuerus
added.note: "In the beginning of his reign" the adversaries write an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.

added.title: Vashti deposed at the feast of Ahasuerus
added.note: In the third year of his reign Ahasuerus makes a feast to his princes for 180 days and seven more for the people of Shushan; Vashti the queen refuses to come at his commandment, and her royal estate is given to another better than she.

added.title: Esther made queen
added.note: Hadassah, Mordecai's cousin whom he had brought up, is taken to the king in the tenth month, Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign; he sets the royal crown on her head. Mordecai, sitting in the king's gate, uncovers the plot of Bigthan and Teresh, and it is written in the chronicles.

added.title: Haman's decree to destroy the Jews
added.note: Mordecai will not bow to Haman the Agagite. In the first month of the twelfth year Pur, the lot, is cast, and letters go out to destroy all the Jews on the thirteenth of Adar. "Who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?" (4:14).

added.title: Esther goes in to the king; Haman hanged
added.note: Esther goes in unbidden and the king holds out the golden sceptre; at her banquet she names Haman, who is hanged on the gallows he made for Mordecai. On the twenty-third of the third month new letters go out, sealed with the king's ring, granting the Jews to stand for their life.

added.title: The Jews delivered; the feast of Purim
added.note: On the thirteenth of Adar, the day their enemies hoped to have power over them, the Jews prevail; the fourteenth and fifteenth are made days of feasting and gladness, Purim, kept by them and their seed for ever. Mordecai is next unto king Ahasuerus, seeking the wealth of his people.

added.title: Reign of Artaxerxes
added.note: Artaxerxes I, Longimanus, son of Xerxes: in his seventh year he sent Ezra (Ezra 7:7), and in his twentieth Nehemiah (Nehemiah 2:1), his years reckoned from the autumn, as the Jews counted them.

added.title: Ezra goes up from Babylon
added.note: In the seventh year of Artaxerxes, Ezra, a ready scribe in the law of Moses, goes up with the king's commission to beautify the house of Yahweh and set magistrates and judges: from the first of the first month to the first of the fifth (7:9), proclaiming a fast at the river Ahava rather than ask the king for soldiers. This commission is the commandment to restore and build Jerusalem from which the seventy weeks are reckoned (Daniel 9:25).

added.title: Ezra's reform: the strange wives put away
added.note: Told that the people, priests and Levites have taken wives of the peoples of the lands, Ezra rends his garment and confesses; on the twentieth of the ninth month, in the great rain, all Judah gathers, and by the first of the first month the strange wives are put away.

added.title: Letter to Artaxerxes: the building of the city stopped
added.note: Rehum and Shimshai write that the Jews are building the rebellious and bad city and setting up its walls; Artaxerxes commands the work to cease, and they make them cease by force and power. Undated in his reign; placed before Nehemiah hears that the wall of Jerusalem is broken down and its gates burned (Nehemiah 1:3).

added.title: Nehemiah hears of Jerusalem's affliction
added.note: In the month Chisleu, in the twentieth year, Hanani tells Nehemiah, the king's cupbearer, of the remnant in great affliction and reproach, and the wall broken down; he weeps, fasts and prays before the God of heaven.

added.title: Nehemiah sent to build the wall
added.note: In the month Nisan, in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes, the king grants Nehemiah letters and timber and sends him as governor; he views the walls by night and says, "Let us rise up and build", while Sanballat and Tobiah laugh them to scorn.

added.title: Nehemiah governor of Judah
added.note: "From the twentieth year even unto the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes the king, that is, twelve years", Nehemiah does not eat the bread of the governor, and makes the nobles restore the lands and the usury they had taken of their brethren (5:14).

added.title: The wall built in fifty and two days
added.note: Every family builds before its own house, half working and half holding spears, every builder with his sword girded; through Sanballat's mockery, threats and plots, the wall is finished on the twenty-fifth of Elul, in fifty and two days, "for they perceived that this work was wrought of our God" (6:16).

added.title: Ezra reads the law; the feast of tabernacles
added.note: On the first of the seventh month Ezra reads the law from morning until midday, and the Levites give the sense; "the joy of Yahweh is your strength" (8:10). They find written that Israel should dwell in booths, and keep the feast as had not been done since the days of Joshua the son of Nun.

added.title: The covenant sealed
added.note: On the twenty-fourth of the seventh month, with fasting and sackcloth, the Levites recount Yahweh's dealings from Abram to the captivity; princes, Levites and priests seal a sure covenant to walk in God's law, keep the sabbath and the seventh year, and not forsake the house of God.

added.title: The wall dedicated
added.note: Two great companies of them that give thanks go upon the wall, one with Ezra and one with Nehemiah, meeting at the house of God, "so that the joy of Jerusalem was heard even afar off" (12:43). Undated; placed after the wall's finishing.

added.title: Nehemiah returns and cleanses the house and the sabbath
added.note: In the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes Nehemiah goes to the king, and after certain days returns to find Tobiah lodged in a chamber of the courts of the house of God. He casts out his stuff, restores the Levites' portions, shuts the gates against the sabbath traffickers and contends with them that had married wives of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab. "Remember me, O my God, for good" (13:31). The last of the Old Testament's history.

added.title: Reign of Darius II
added.note: Darius the Persian, under whom the Levites and priests were recorded (Nehemiah 12:22), taken as Darius II, son of Artaxerxes: the last Persian king the Old Testament names.

added.title: Lifetime of Jeremiah
added.note: Scripture gives no age for Jeremiah. He was a child when called in the thirteenth year of Josiah (Jeremiah 1:2, 6), so born about 648, and he is last seen carried into Egypt with the remnant after Gedaliah was slain (Jeremiah 43). When he died is not recorded; the bar runs to an estimated lifespan of about seventy years.

added.title: Lifetime of Ezekiel
added.note: "In the thirtieth year", the fifth year of king Jehoiachin's captivity (Ezekiel 1:1-2), taken as Ezekiel's age when he was called, as a priest entered his service at thirty (Numbers 4:3): so born about 623. His last dated word is in the seven and twentieth year (Ezekiel 29:17). When he died is not recorded; the bar runs to an estimated lifespan of about seventy years.

added.title: Lifetime of Daniel
added.note: Daniel was one of the "children" of royal seed carried away in the third year of Jehoiakim (Daniel 1:1-4), taken here as about fifteen: so born about 621. He is last seen in the third year of Cyrus (Daniel 10:1), told "go thou thy way till the end be: for thou shalt rest, and stand in thy lot at the end of the days" (12:13).

added.title: Lifetime of Jehoiachin (Jeconiah)
added.note: Eighteen years old when he began to reign, three months before he was carried to Babylon (2 Kings 24:8): so born in 615. Released from prison by Evil-merodach in the seven and thirtieth year of his captivity, he ate bread before the king "all the days of his life" (25:29). When he died is not recorded; the bar runs to an estimated sixty years.

added.title: Lifetime of Jeshua
added.note: Jeshua (Joshua) the high priest, son of Jozadak, who went into captivity when Jerusalem fell (1 Chronicles 6:15): so born in exile, here taken as about 580. He came up with Zerubbabel, built the altar, and is last seen crowned in Zechariah's sign of the BRANCH in the second year of Darius (Zechariah 6:11). When he died is not recorded; the bar runs to an estimated lifespan of about seventy years.

added.title: Lifetime of Zerubbabel
added.note: Grandson of Jehoiachin, whose sons were born in captivity (1 Chronicles 3:17-19): so born about 570. He led the first return and laid the foundation of the house, and is last seen in the second year of Darius, when Yahweh said "I will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee" (Haggai 2:23). When he died is not recorded; the bar runs to an estimated lifespan of about seventy years.

added.title: Lifetime of Mordecai
added.note: Scripture gives no age for Mordecai. With Ahasuerus taken as Xerxes, the one carried away with Jeconiah (Esther 2:6) is his great-grandfather Kish, and Mordecai, a man of standing at the king's gate by 478, is taken as born about 520. He is last seen next unto king Ahasuerus, "seeking the wealth of his people" (10:3). When he died is not recorded; the bar runs to an estimated lifespan of about seventy years.

added.title: Lifetime of Ezra
added.note: Scripture gives no age for Ezra. A ready scribe and priest when he went up in the seventh year of Artaxerxes (Ezra 7:6-7), here taken as about forty-five: so born about 502. He is last seen leading the company at the dedication of the wall (Nehemiah 12:36). When he died is not recorded; the bar runs to an estimated lifespan of about seventy years.

added.title: Lifetime of Esther
added.note: Scripture gives no age for Esther. A young virgin when gathered to Shushan and made queen in the seventh year of Ahasuerus (Esther 2:8, 16), here taken as about twenty: so born about 498. She is last seen confirming the days of Purim (9:29-32). When she died is not recorded; the bar runs to an estimated lifespan of about seventy years.

added.title: Lifetime of Nehemiah
added.note: Scripture gives no age for Nehemiah. The king's cupbearer in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes (Nehemiah 1:11, 2:1), here taken as about thirty-five: so born about 480. He is last seen cleansing the house and the sabbath after the two and thirtieth year (13:6-31). When he died is not recorded; the bar runs to an estimated lifespan of about seventy years.

names.why: A word of the name, Lot, finds Lot himself; TIPNR has no record of his daughters.
Ptolemais is Acco (Acts 21:7), as in journeys.json.
